about: Phase-line parse cases shared by engine/tests/test_possessive_phase.py (the Python statement of the rule) and web/scripts/replay_phase.test.mjs (which runs web/lib/replay.ts parsePhase). Synthetic deck names, no real decklist. `p` is the player key the line belongs to, `label` the phase with the possessive removed.

cases.why: possessive deck name: the playtester's bug
cases.label: Main phase, precombat

cases.why: possessive name that also ends in s, so Forge writes a bare apostrophe
cases.label: Declare Blockers Step

cases.why: plain name ending in s (control: the old regex read this right)
cases.label: Upkeep step

cases.why: line without the seat prefix, keys with it
cases.label: Declare Attackers Step

cases.why: line with the seat prefix, keys without it
cases.label: End step

cases.why: longest first: a seat named Skrat must not claim Skrat's Revenge's line
cases.label: Cleanup step

cases.why: longest first still lets the shorter seat have its own line
cases.label: Upkeep step

cases.why: mirror match: the seat prefix decides which copy of the deck
cases.label: Draw step

cases.why: upper-case name ending in S: both possessive forms accepted
cases.label: Combat Damage Step

cases.why: name ending in s written with 's
cases.label: End of Combat Step

cases.why: no known keys: the old regex is the fallback, fine for a plain name
cases.label: Untap step

cases.why: no known keys: the fallback still misreads an apostrophe, which is why it is only a fallback
cases.label: Revenge's Untap step
